name_en: Ahodaki — desalted old takuan pickle simmered in soy sauce
summary_ja: 味や匂いが落ちてきた古漬けのたくあんを塩抜きし、醤油だれで炊き直す北勢地域の常備菜。美味しい時期を過ぎてから食べる「あほなことをしている」との自嘲めいた名の由来が伝わる、食品を無駄にしない知恵の料理。
summary_en: Old takuan pickle, once its flavor and aroma have faded, is desalted and simmered again in soy sauce, a pantry staple from the Hokusei area. Its name — playfully self-deprecating, roughly "doing a foolish thing" — nods to eating it well past its prime, a frugal way to waste nothing.

name_en: Sakana no shiokara — whole fish salted and cured for months
summary_ja: イワシやサンマ、サバ、カツオなどを一匹丸ごと塩で漬け込み、秋から冬に仕込んで春に食べる保存食。冷蔵庫のない時代、熊野灘の好漁場で大量にとれた魚を余さず活かす知恵として伝わってきたという。
summary_en: Whole sardine, saury, mackerel, or bonito are packed in salt and cured for months, typically salted in autumn or winter and eaten in spring. Born before refrigeration, the practice made full use of the abundant catch from the rich fishing grounds off the Kumano-nada coast.
source_title: 魚の漬物（塩辛） 三重県
